text:
tess: noticed an uptick in unassigned inbound leads during the afternoon spike. looks related to enrichment timeouts + hubspot throttling.

harry: yeah we saw a 429 burst from HubSpot API around 1775556400. enrichment retrier didn't respect Retry-After header. that left leads in limbo and RR didn't rotate new owners.

gloria: yikes. current policy ignores Retry-After to maintain low-latency attempts. maybe we should respect it but use delayed requeue into a jittered backlog to avoid losing throughput.

tess: proposed change: honor Retry-After, and when present, put lead into delayed queue with exponential backoff + jitter; also set a fast-path that if delayed queue length > 50, escalate to overflow-owner immediately.

harry: config proposal: 
```
respect_retry_after: true
delayed_queue_backoff_base_s: 2
delayed_queue_max_retries: 5
delayed_queue_overflow_threshold: 50
overflow_email: "marketing-ops@redwood.com"
```

ops-bot: added a dashboard panel for delayed-queue length and 429 rate.

gloria: also add a small change to round-robin: when lead has partial enrichment (email ok, company missing), allow RR assignment but tag lead with "needs-company-enrich" so SF sync can try enrichment later. avoids dropping leads that are still actionable.

tess: test plan: simulate 429s in staging for 15m, validate delayed queue drain and overflow escalation. also run canary of RR behavior for 1 hour.

harry: I'll open a quick PR and ping @devex for docs update on playbook.

sales-ping-bot: FYI @sales - temporary change may route some leads to marketing-ops overflow during the test window.

ops-bot: alert created: delayed-queue > 50 will trigger #marketing channel post.

gloria: if staging looks good, we'll ship the config at 0300 to reduce customer impact.

tess: thanks all. small change but should cut unassigned leads by 80% during spikes.

harry: pr: github.com/redwood/leadflow/pull/1829

ops-bot: patch deployed to staging canary :white_check_mark:
